literal: Profit desiring, capital which loses undertaking, will not undertake the wise.
translation: The wise will not undertake an action that risks the capital in the hope of making a profit.
modern: லாபத்தை விரும்பி இருக்கும் முதலையும் இழக்கச் செய்யும் செயல்களை அறிவுடையவர்கள் தொடங்க மாட்டார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet warns against reckless ventures. It states that wise people will not engage in actions that might destroy their initial capital just because they desire a potential profit. The word mutal refers to the base capital or existing resources, while aakkam denotes the expected gain. True wisdom lies in protecting what one already has before attempting to multiply it.
